clue.text: Hiatus caused by airman — a foreign one

parts.note: LAC is the abbreviation for leading aircraftman, a junior RAF rank
una is 'a' or 'one' in Italian and Spanish

explanation.surface: A gap in proceedings is blamed on some visiting pilot from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link; the definition is the first word. LAC (leading aircraftman, a rank in Britain's Royal Air Force) is followed by UNA, the feminine 'a' or 'one' in Italian or Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a gap or missing section, so it is a break or pause much like a hiatus.

clue.text: Heard when judged the ultimate winner

explanation.surface: The final champion is announced once the judges have decided.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet blast heard at the Day of Judgment; and the final winning card of a hand in bridge or whist.

clue.text: Explain how to make profit on a horse

parts.note: to clear a sum is to make it as net profit
a jockey who is up is riding a horse

explanation.surface: Advice on how to win money backing a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how to' is a link. CLEAR (net a profit) plus UP, as a jockey is 'up' when riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mystery is to resolve or account for it, which is to explain it.

clue.text: Send rights issue for late investment

indicators.note: an issue of shares is a putting out, here read as the letters coming out in new order

explanation.surface: A company launches a rights issue to raise money for a late investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' rearranges SEND RIGHTS. 'investment' is a garment you are invested in, and it is worn late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is clothing for wearing in bed, so it is a garment donned late in the day.

clue.text: Square pole in desert quarter

parts.note: a quad is a college square or quadrangle

indicators.note: in tells us the pole letter sits inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
N stands for the north pole

explanation.surface: A square with a pole standing in a desert district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun meaning sandy waste, but here it is a verb: to abandon. 'in' puts the pole inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, one of four equal sectors.

clue.text: Went up and down from university — left in no time!

indicators.note: in says the university and left letters sit inside the phrase for no time

parts.note: undated means bearing no time or date

explanation.surface: Someone bounced away from college and left in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in no time' reads as 'instantly', but it says U and L go inside UNDATED (with no date).
explanation.definitionFit: Undulated means moved in waves, rising and falling like the sea.

clue.text: Quick notes in succession at end of movement

parts.note: D, E and F are consecutive notes of the musical scale

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word movement

explanation.surface: A rapid run of notes rounds off a musical movement.
explanation.walkthrough: D, E, F are three consecutive musical notes, then the last letter of 'movement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means nimble and skilful, so it fits a quick pair of hands.

clue.text: Place of work that is later demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A workplace that will be knocked down later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges IE (i.e., 'that is') with LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workshop.

clue.text: Painter without one god

indicators.note: without says a letter for one is dropped from the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An artist bereft of a single deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from TITIAN, the Venetian painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant deities of Greek myth who preceded the Olympians.

clue.text: Gaol disturbance

explanation.surface: Trouble in the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for prison, as in doing time inside; and a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Cunning verbal snub

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym of snub

parts.note: a slight is a snub or deliberate insult

explanation.surface: A sly remark that puts someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal' is the homophone signal: the answer is said exactly like SLIGHT, a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or craft, as in sleight of hand, so it means artful cunning as a noun.

clue.text: Fed up Celt goes round bend

indicators.note: in a down-style reading, up says the word Fed is turned backwards
goes round says the letters of Celt are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A Celtic man, sick of it all, is driven round the bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like one idiom meaning annoyed, but 'up' turns 'Fed' backwards, giving DEF, and 'goes round' rearranges 'Celt', giving LECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect is to turn something aside from its course, so it means to make it bend away.

clue.text: Left in utter confusion after gybe, and capsize

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled part behind the word for gybe

parts.note: to gybe is to turn a sailing boat so the boom swings across

indicators.note: confusion says the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sailor botches a gybe and the dinghy goes over in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' rearranges L with 'utter'. To turn turtle is to flip upside down, like a turtle stranded on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is an idiom for a boat overturning so that its hull faces the sky.

clue.text: One entering workers carriage

indicators.note: entering says the letter for one goes inside the word for workers

parts.note: men are workers or hands, as on a factory floor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single person boards a coach meant for staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' looks like a railway vehicle but means bearing or deportment. The page prints 'workers'' with an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or manner, the same sense as the way one holds oneself.

clue.text: "The Iron Hand" — Poe's prison version

indicators.note: version means a reworked form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped and the S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A title for Edgar Allan Poe's own account of jail life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges POES and PRISON; the S of the possessive counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannical, harsh rule is often called an iron hand, so the phrase stands for heavy-handed domination.

clue.text: They give out good notes, after some hesitation

indicators.note: after says the good notes follow the hesitation

parts.note: um is the noise of someone hesitating
pi is short for pious, hence good
re is a note of the sol-fa scale, so res are notes

explanation.surface: Teachers hand out good marks only after some dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give out' suggests distributing, but in cricket the officials give a batter out. UM, then PI (pious), then RES (more than one re, the sol-fa note).
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires are the officials who rule a cricket batter dismissed by raising a finger.

clue.text: Thus getting Russian agreement to dilute the drink

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
da is Russian for yes
to water a drink is to dilute it

explanation.surface: A Russian consents to having the drink watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'to' join the pieces: SO, DA (Russian 'yes') and WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated water, a fizzy mixer for spirits.

clue.text: Reduced bureaucracy, switching the sides round

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places, the front going to the back

parts.note: red tape is bureaucratic red-tape procedure

explanation.surface: Bureaucracy has been cut back by reversing the policies of both parties.
explanation.walkthrough: RED TAPE with its two halves swapped gives TAPE + RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapered means narrowed or diminished gradually, so it means reduced.

clue.text: Reckless, some French exercise speed

parts.note: des is the French for some
PE is physical education, school exercise
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Some French people work out at a frantic pace.
explanation.walkthrough: DES ('some' in French), PE (physical education), RATE (speed).
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate can mean rash or careless of danger through having nothing to lose.

clue.text: Drafted under stress

explanation.surface: Conscripted while overwhelmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafted, as in press-ganged into the navy; and under stress, as in hard-up for time or harried.

clue.text: Withdraw out of region

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or from
a tract is a region or stretch of land

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a territory.
explanation.walkthrough: EX (Latin 'out of') followed by TRACT (an expanse of land).
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull something out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Makes obscure studies about where the Tables of the Law were kept

indicators.note: about means the word for studies is wrapped round the vessel

parts.note: dens are studies, private rooms for work

parts.words: where the Tables of the Law were kept
parts.note: the Ark of the Covenant held the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments

explanation.surface: A scholar clouds the issue by researching where the commandments were stored.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tables of the Law are the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments, which the Bible says were kept in the Ark of the Covenant; 'about' wraps the studies round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken something is to make it dimmer or harder to see, so it obscures it.

clue.text: Hair bouffant, to our delight

indicators.note: bouffant means puffed out, so the letters of the hair are fluffed into a new order

parts.note: a mane is a long thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A big puffed-up hairdo, much to our pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouffant' (puffed-up, of a hairstyle) rearranges the hair word into ENAM; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to charm or captivate someone, which is to delight them.

clue.text: Essential part for this kind of helmet

explanation.surface: The heart of the matter is what this colonial headgear is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or gist of a matter; and the cork-like plant tissue that tropical sun helmets were made from.

clue.text: Pinch some cheesecake

parts.note: the answer read as an instruction, the first three letters written upward, gives nip, which means pinch

explanation.surface: Stealing a slice of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: in a down entry PIN read 'up' is NIP, which is 'Pinch'. 'Cheesecake' is old slang for glamour photos.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is slang for glamour photography of women, and a poster girl picture of that kind is a pin-up.

clue.text: Clear ante-post betting transaction

indicators.note: ante is Latin for before, so the first word comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to sweep is to clear, as a broom clears a floor
a stake is a wooden post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A clean-cut bet placed in advance of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ante-post' looks like the racing term for bets laid before race day, but split it: 'ante' is Latin for before, putting the clearing word before the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a gamble where all the stakes go into one pot paid out to the winner.

clue.text: Quarters with inner city style

indicators.note: with inner says the city goes inside the pair of quarters

parts.note: E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Housing with a stylish inner-city flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: LA (Los Angeles) goes between E and N, two compass points or quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash or flair, a vigorous stylishness.

clue.text: Oh! This I don't believe

parts.note: the word that completes a sceptical 'Oh ...!' of disbelief, used ironically to mean the opposite of yes

explanation.surface: An exclamation of flat disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Ob!', a misprint for 'Oh!'. Said with irony, 'Oh, yeah!' means 'I don't believe that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken sarcastically, this informal yes signals doubt rather than agreement.

clue.text: Most fastidious goddess in a haunt of thieves

indicators.note: in places the goddess inside the word for a thieves' haunt

parts.note: a nest is a den or hideout of thieves
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: The fussiest goddess turns up among a gang of robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin; the den is the nest of the phrase 'a nest of thieves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning most tidy and particular about order.

clue.text: State in North Australia, brought back in song

indicators.note: the second in places the turned letters inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: brought back says the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Oz is the slang name for Australia

explanation.surface: A ballad brings an American state to the north of Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses north plus Oz, giving ZON. The first 'in' belongs to the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the south-west.

clue.text: Small baseball players with long ears?

definitions.text: Small baseball players with long ears?

parts.words: Small baseball players with long ears?
parts.note: baseball throwers, and also jugs with handles, recalling the proverb that little jugs have big ears, meaning children overhear

explanation.surface: Diminutive athletes with long ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'little pitchers have big ears' warns that children overhear; a pitcher is a jug whose handle is its ear, and also a baseball thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball's throwers and large handled jugs share one name; the ears are the jug handles.

clue.text: One badly spoken is certainly not correct

parts.note: 'un is a slangy, clipped way of saying one, as in a good 'un
true! is an exclamation meaning certainly, quite so

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks poorly is definitely wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly spoken' is not a homophone signal here: it describes the dialect form 'UN. TRUE, as in 'True!', agrees with 'certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means false, so it describes something that is wrong or mistaken.
